newsitem.title: UK: AMEC shares open higher after results.
newsitem.headline: AMEC shares open higher after results.

text.p: Shares in AMEC Plc climbed on Thursday as the company reported annual profits at the top end of expectations and said there were signs that the UK construction market was improving.
Shares in the engineering and construction group were up three pence at 130 by 0835 GMT.
AMEC announced a 71 percent surge in 1996 pre-tax, pre-exceptional profits to 37.7 million stg. Analysts forecasts had ranged from 35 to 38 million.
"The results were pretty encouraging and the shares have reacted accordingly," one market maker said.
AMEC proposed a total dividend of four pence per share, up from three pence in 1995.

"It is pleasing to be able to announce pre-tax profits up 71 percent accompanied by further improvements in the group's cash position and a dividend increased by 33 percent. This level of increase demonstrates our confidence going forward," group chief executive Peter Mason said in a statement.

Mason said that in the 14 months since joining the company, the management structure had been reorganised, its housing subsidiary had been revitalised, 75 million pounds had been realised through disposals and it had transformed its international presence.
"My strategic review continues. We have made some positive progress, but I can see more that has to be done and in the coming months it will be done," he said.
